claim: Induction of intestinal drug metabolizing enzymes can complicate the development of new drugs, owing to the potential to cause drug-drug interactions (DDIs) leading to changes in pharmacokinetics, safety and efficacy.
source: Induction of intestinal drug metabolizing enzymes can complicate the development of new drugs, owing to the potential to cause drug-drug interactions (DDIs) leading to changes in pharmacokinetics, safety and efficacy.
evidence: This is a statement about the impact of enzyme induction on drug development, drawing from established knowledge in pharmacology.

claim: Species differences preclude extrapolation from animals for predicting CYP450 induction in humans.
source: The development of a human-relevant model of the adult intestine that accurately predicts CYP450 induction could help address this challenge as species differences preclude extrapolation from animals.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about species differences in drug metabolism.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip demonstrates polarized cell architecture.
source: Duodenum Intestine-Chip demonstrates the polarized cell architecture, intestinal barrier function, presence of specialized cell subpopulations, and in vivo relevant expression, localization, and function of major intestinal drug transporters.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations described in the manuscript, including immunofluorescence imaging and morphological analysis.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip demonstrates intestinal barrier function.
source: Duodenum Intestine-Chip demonstrates the polarized cell architecture, intestinal barrier function, presence of specialized cell subpopulations, and in vivo relevant expression, localization, and function of major intestinal drug transporters.
evidence: This is supported by permeability assay data showing low Papp values for dextran.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip demonstrates presence of specialized cell subpopulations.
source: Duodenum Intestine-Chip demonstrates the polarized cell architecture, intestinal barrier function, presence of specialized cell subpopulations, and in vivo relevant expression, localization, and function of major intestinal drug transporters.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining and gene expression analysis showing multiple intestinal cell types.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip demonstrates in vivo relevant expression, localization, and function of major intestinal drug transporters.
source: Duodenum Intestine-Chip demonstrates the polarized cell architecture, intestinal barrier function, presence of specialized cell subpopulations, and in vivo relevant expression, localization, and function of major intestinal drug transporters.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data, immunofluorescence imaging, and functional assays for drug transporters.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip displays improved CYP3A4 expression compared to Caco-2.
source: Notably, in comparison to Caco-2, it displays improved CYP3A4 expression and induction capability.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR and western blot data showing higher CYP3A4 levels in Duodenum Intestine-Chip.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip displays improved CYP3A4 induction capability compared to Caco-2.
source: Notably, in comparison to Caco-2, it displays improved CYP3A4 expression and induction capability.
evidence: This is supported by data showing CYP3A4 induction in response to rifampicin and vitamin D3 treatment.

claim: High affinity of certain drugs for cellular transporters combined with the extensive activity of metabolic enzymes present in the human intestine are the main factors limiting drug bioavailability.
source: High affinity of certain drugs for cellular transporters combined with the extensive activity of metabolic enzymes present in the human intestine are the main factors limiting drug bioavailability (Dietrich, 2003; Thummel, 2007; Shugarts and Benet, 2009; Peters et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Hepatic drug clearance is well-understood and relatively well predicted by pre-clinical models.
source: After decades of research, the hepatic drug clearance is well-understood and relatively well predicted by pre-clinical models, while the accurate prediction of the first-pass extraction of xenobiotics in human intestinal epithelium still remains elusive.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge in the field of pharmacology.

claim: Accurate prediction of the first-pass extraction of xenobiotics in human intestinal epithelium still remains elusive.
source: After decades of research, the hepatic drug clearance is well-understood and relatively well predicted by pre-clinical models, while the accurate prediction of the first-pass extraction of xenobiotics in human intestinal epithelium still remains elusive.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about limitations in current models.

claim: Species differences in the isoforms, regional abundances, differences in substrate specificity of drug metabolism enzymes preclude accurate extrapolation of the data from animal models to the clinic.
source: Species differences in the isoforms, regional abundances, differences in substrate specificity of drug metabolism enzymes (Martignoni et al., 2006; Paine et al., 2006; Komura and Iwaki, 2011) and transporters (Tucker et al., 2012; Gröer et al., 2013), and mechanism regulating transcriptional activation (LeCluyse, 2001; Mackowiak et al., 2018), precludes accurate extrapolation of the data from animal models to the clinic.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: In mice, there are 34 cytochrome P450 (CYPs) in the major gene families involved in drug metabolism.
source: In mice, for example, there are 34 cytochrome P450 (CYPs) in the major gene families involved in drug metabolism, that is the CYP1A, CYP2C, CYP2D, and CYP3A gene clusters, while in humans, there are only eight (Nelson et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In humans, there are only eight cytochrome P450 (CYPs) in the major gene families involved in drug metabolism.
source: In mice, for example, there are 34 cytochrome P450 (CYPs) in the major gene families involved in drug metabolism, that is the CYP1A, CYP2C, CYP2D, and CYP3A gene clusters, while in humans, there are only eight (Nelson et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Three human enzymes, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4, account for approximately 75% of all drug metabolism reactions.
source: Interestingly, three human enzymes, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4, account for ∼75% of all reactions, with CYP3A4 being the single most important human CYP450 accounting for ∼45% of phase one drug metabolism in humans (Guengerich, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: CYP3A4 accounts for approximately 45% of phase one drug metabolism in humans.
source: Interestingly, three human enzymes, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4, account for ∼75% of all reactions, with CYP3A4 being the single most important human CYP450 accounting for ∼45% of phase one drug metabolism in humans (Guengerich, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Rifampicin and SR12813 are potent agonists for human PXR (hPXR) but not for mouse PXR (mPXR).
source: For example, rifampicin and SR12813 are potent agonists for human PXR (hPXR) but not for mouse PXR (mPXR), whereas the potent mPXR agonist 5-pregnen-3β-ol-20-one-16α-carbonitrile (PCN) is a poor agonist for hPXR (Kliewer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: PCN is a potent mPXR agonist but a poor agonist for hPXR.
source: For example, rifampicin and SR12813 are potent agonists for human PXR (hPXR) but not for mouse PXR (mPXR), whereas the potent mPXR agonist 5-pregnen-3β-ol-20-one-16α-carbonitrile (PCN) is a poor agonist for hPXR (Kliewer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: CITCO is a strong agonist for human CAR (hCAR) but not mouse CAR (mCAR).
source: On the other hand, 6-(4-chlorophenyl)imidazo[2,1-b][1,3]thiazole-5-carbaldehyde-O-(3,4-dichlorobenzyl)oxime (CITCO) is a strong agonist for human CAR (hCAR) but not mouse CAR (mCAR) (Maglich et al., 2003), while 1,4-bis-[2-(3,5-dichloropyridyloxy)]benzene,3,3′,5,5′-tetrachloro-1,4-bis(pyridyloxy)benzene (TCPOBOP) is more selective for mCAR than hCAR.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: TCPOBOP is more selective for mCAR than hCAR.
source: On the other hand, 6-(4-chlorophenyl)imidazo[2,1-b][1,3]thiazole-5-carbaldehyde-O-(3,4-dichlorobenzyl)oxime (CITCO) is a strong agonist for human CAR (hCAR) but not mouse CAR (mCAR) (Maglich et al., 2003), while 1,4-bis-[2-(3,5-dichloropyridyloxy)]benzene,3,3′,5,5′-tetrachloro-1,4-bis(pyridyloxy)benzene (TCPOBOP) is more selective for mCAR than hCAR.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Caco-2 monolayer culture on a transwell insert is one of the most widely used models across the pharmaceutical industry as an in vitro representation of the human small intestine.
source: Among these is a Caco-2 monolayer culture on a transwell insert, which is one of the most widely used models across the pharmaceutical industry as an in vitro representation of the human small intestine.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge in the pharmaceutical industry.

claim: Caco-2 models have inherent limitations including lack of in vivo relevant three-dimensional (3D) cytoarchitecture, lack of appropriate ratio of cell populations, altered expression profiles of drug transporters and drug metabolizing enzymes, especially CYP450s, and aberrant CYP450-induction response.
source: However, inherent limitations, such as lack of in vivo relevant three-dimensional (3D) cytoarchitecture, lack of appropriate ratio of cell populations, altered expression profiles of drug transporters and drug metabolizing enzymes, especially CYP450s, and aberrant CYP450-induction response, challenge the use of these model for predicting human responses in the clinic (Sun et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Organoids derived from all regions of the intestinal tract can be established.
source: Using these methods, organoids derived from all regions of the intestinal tract can be established (Sato et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2015) and applied into different areas of research including organ development, disease modeling, and regenerative medicine (Fatehullah et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The 3D spherical architecture of the organoid restricts access to its lumen, which is crucial for assessing intestinal permeability or drug absorption.
source: The 3D spherical architecture of the organoid restricts access to its lumen, which is crucial for assessing intestinal permeability or drug absorption.
evidence: This is based on logical inference from the structural characteristics of organoids.

claim: Exposure of the apical cell surface of intestinal organoid to compounds requires the use of time-consuming and labor-intensive procedures, such as microinjection.
source: Indeed, exposure of the apical cell surface of intestinal organoid to compounds requires the use of time-consuming and labor-intensive procedures, such as microinjection.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about organoid methodology.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip provides a human-relevant model for the studies of drug transport, drug metabolism, and DDIs.
source: Here, we demonstrated that Duodenum Intestine-Chip provides a human-relevant model for the studies of drug transport, drug metabolism, and DDIs, which is much closer to the human tissue, compared to organoids, as supported by the comparison of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) expression profiles.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data comparing gene expression profiles.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip is much closer to human tissue compared to organoids, as supported by RNA sequencing expression profiles.
source: Here, we demonstrated that Duodenum Intestine-Chip provides a human-relevant model for the studies of drug transport, drug metabolism, and DDIs, which is much closer to the human tissue, compared to organoids, as supported by the comparison of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) expression profiles.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing closer similarity to human duodenal tissue.

claim: Presence of mechanical forces in Duodenum Intestine-Chip improves the formation of polarized cytoarchitecture.
source: Presence of the mechanical forces, which we apply in this system in order to recapitulate the blood flow and shear stress, showed to improve the formation of polarized cytoarchitecture and the appearance of intestinal microvilli on the apical cell surface.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging and SEM data comparing static and flow conditions.

claim: Presence of mechanical forces in Duodenum Intestine-Chip improves the appearance of intestinal microvilli on the apical cell surface.
source: Presence of the mechanical forces, which we apply in this system in order to recapitulate the blood flow and shear stress, showed to improve the formation of polarized cytoarchitecture and the appearance of intestinal microvilli on the apical cell surface.
evidence: This is supported by SEM data showing increased microvilli density under flow conditions.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip supported successful maturation of all major intestinal epithelial cell types in the physiologically relevant ratios.
source: In addition, Duodenum Intestine-Chip supported successful maturation of all major intestinal epithelial cell types in the physiologically relevant ratios and demonstrated low paracellular permeability.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining and quantitative image analysis data.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip demonstrated low paracellular permeability.
source: In addition, Duodenum Intestine-Chip supported successful maturation of all major intestinal epithelial cell types in the physiologically relevant ratios and demonstrated low paracellular permeability.
evidence: This is supported by permeability assay data showing low Papp values.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip showed closer to in vivo expression of drug uptake and efflux transporters, as compared to Intestine-Chip developed with Caco-2 cells.
source: Importantly for its use in pharmacokinetic studies, it showed closer to in vivo expression of drug uptake and efflux transporters, as compared to Intestine-Chip developed with Caco-2 cells.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data comparing transporter expression levels.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip exhibits the correct luminal localization and functional activity of MDR1 (P-gp).
source: Additionally, we were able to show that the Duodenum Intestine-Chip exhibits the correct luminal localization and functional activity of MDR1 (P-gp), and supports high expression of the cytochrome CYP450 (CYP) 3A4 - close to the levels observed in the human duodenal tissue.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging and functional assay data.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip supports high expression of CYP3A4 close to the levels observed in the human duodenal tissue.
source: Additionally, we were able to show that the Duodenum Intestine-Chip exhibits the correct luminal localization and functional activity of MDR1 (P-gp), and supports high expression of the cytochrome CYP450 (CYP) 3A4 - close to the levels observed in the human duodenal tissue.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR and western blot data.

claim: Exposure of the Duodenum Intestine-Chip to rifampicin resulted in significantly increased CYP3A4 mRNA, protein levels, and drug metabolism activity.
source: Importantly, exposure of the Duodenum Intestine-Chip to known CYP450 inducers in humans, such as rifampicin and 1, 25-dihydroxyvitamin D3, resulted in significantly increased CYP3A4 mRNA, protein levels, and drug metabolism activity.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR, western blot, and enzyme activity assay data.

claim: Exposure of the Duodenum Intestine-Chip to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 resulted in significantly increased CYP3A4 mRNA, protein levels, and drug metabolism activity.
source: Importantly, exposure of the Duodenum Intestine-Chip to known CYP450 inducers in humans, such as rifampicin and 1, 25-dihydroxyvitamin D3, resulted in significantly increased CYP3A4 mRNA, protein levels, and drug metabolism activity.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR, western blot, and enzyme activity assay data.

claim: Organoid-derived intestinal cells can be combined with Organs-on-Chips technology to provide a robust and human-relevant system for preclinical assessment of CYP450-mediated metabolism, activity of drug transporters, and the potential risk of DDIs.
source: Our results indicate that the organoid-derived intestinal cells can be combined with Organs-on-Chips technology to provide a robust and human-relevant system for preclinical assessment of CYP450-mediated metabolism, activity of drug transporters, and the potential risk of DDIs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined results of the study.

claim: Organoid cultures were established from crypts isolated from endoscopic biopsies of three different healthy adult individuals.
source: In brief, we first established organoid cultures (Figure 1A; top) from crypts isolated from endoscopic biopsies of three different healthy adult individuals, the organoids were then dissociated into fragments and seeded on the top of the Extracellular Matrix (ECM)-coated porous flexible polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) membrane of the chips (Figure 1B; 3: indicates the epithelial tissue).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Primary human intestinal microvascular endothelial cells (HIMECs) were used to populate the vascular channel of the chip.
source: Primary human intestinal microvascular endothelial cells (HIMECs, Cell Biologics), derived from the human small intestine (Figure 1A; bottom), were used to populate the other surface of the PDMS membrane in the vascular channel (Figure 1B; 4: indicates the endothelial cells).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip was perfused continuously through the luminal and vascular compartment with fresh cell culture medium.
source: Next, the Duodenum Intestine-Chip was perfused continuously through the luminal and vascular compartment with fresh cell culture medium.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Epithelial monolayers in Duodenum Intestine-Chip were subjected to cyclic mechanical strain (10% strain, 0.2 Hz) to emulate physiologically relevant forces of intestinal peristalsis.
source: Once the epithelial monolayers reached confluency they were subjected to cyclic mechanical strain (10% strain, 0.2 Hz) in order to emulate physiologically relevant forces of intestinal peristalsis.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Exposure of the Duodenum Intestine-Chip to flow for 72 hr resulted in accelerated polarization of the epithelial cells and formation of apical microvilli.
source: Exposure of the Duodenum Intestine-Chip to flow for 72 hr resulted in accelerated polarization of the epithelial cells and formation of apical microvilli (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), what is in line with our previous findings reported for the Caco-2 cells (Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging and SEM data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cells cultured under static conditions resulted in the formation of a monolayer of flat (14.8 ± 2.6 μm) squamous cells with poorly defined cell-cell junctions.
source: We observed that culture of primary intestinal epithelial cells in the chips maintained under static conditions resulted in the formation of a monolayer of flat (14.8 ± 2.6 μm) squamous cells with poorly defined cell-cell junctions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and sparsely distributed microvilli (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cells cultured under flow (30 μl/hr) with or without concomitant application of cyclic stretch (10% strain, 0.2 Hz), exhibited a well-polarized and cobblestone-like morphology with increased cell height (27.0 ± 1.3 μm), strongly delineated junctions, and densely packed microvilli.
source: In contrast, cells cultured under flow (30 μl/hr) with or without concomitant application of cyclic stretch (10% strain, 0.2 Hz), exhibited a well-polarized and cobblestone-like morphology with increased cell height (27.0 ± 1.3 μm), strongly delineated junctions, and densely packed microvilli.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging and SEM data.

claim: Application of constant flow (shear stress) was critical for promoting maturation of a well-polarized epithelium.
source: In line with our previous observations, application of the constant flow (shear stress) was critical for promoting maturation of a well-polarized epithelium, while short-term application of cyclic strain did not show any additional effect.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of different culture conditions.

claim: Short-term application of cyclic strain did not show any additional effect on epithelial maturation beyond flow alone.
source: In line with our previous observations, application of the constant flow (shear stress) was critical for promoting maturation of a well-polarized epithelium, while short-term application of cyclic strain did not show any additional effect.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of different culture conditions.

claim: Prolonged cell exposure to flow and cyclic strain resulted in the spontaneous development (around day 6 of culture) of epithelial undulations ('villi-like structures') extending into the lumen of the epithelial channel.
source: Moreover, prolonged cell exposure to flow and cyclic strain resulted in the spontaneous development (around day 6 of culture) of epithelial undulations ('villi-like structures') extending into the lumen of the epithelial channel and covered by continuous brush border (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by SEM data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Culture conditions in Duodenum Intestine-Chip resulted in a time-dependent improvement of intestinal barrier function as indicated by the low permeability coefficient (Papp) of fluorescently labeled dextran.
source: Importantly, these culture conditions resulted in a time-dependent improvement of intestinal permeability as indicated by the low permeability coefficient (Papp) of fluorescently labeled dextran recorded in the Duodenum Intestine-Chip generated from organoid-derived cells of three different individuals (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by permeability assay data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Expression of alkaline phosphatase and mucin 2 reached levels similar to those detected in RNA isolated directly from the human duodenal tissue on day 8 of chip culture.
source: As shown in Figure 2A, expression of most of the markers tested, with the exception of lysozyme, increased over time in culture. Notably, on day 8 of chip culture the mRNA expression of alkaline phosphatase and mucin two reached levels similar to those detected in RNA isolated directly from the human duodenal tissue.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Lysozyme expression showed a declining trend over time in culture suggesting a reduction in Paneth cell population.
source: Lysozyme expression showed the opposite trend (declined expression over time in culture) suggesting a reduction in Paneth cell population, which is in line with the observed increased differentiation of the villus epithelium and decreased stemness.
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression data and knowledge of intestinal cell biology.

claim: The relative abundance of intestinal cell types within the chips is similar to their ratios observed in in vivo tissue.
source: In addition, immunostaining followed by quantitative image analysis confirmed the presence of all major differentiated intestinal epithelial cell types and revealed that the relative abundance of these cell types within the chips is similar to their ratios observed in in vivo tissue (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging and quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The ratios of absorptive enterocytes, goblet cells, enteroendocrine and Paneth cells observed in the chips on day 8 of fluidic culture were close to those reported following histopathological evaluation of sections from normal human duodenum.
source: Indeed, the ratios of absorptive enterocytes, goblet cells, enteroendocrine and Paneth cells observed in the chips on day 8 of fluidic culture, were close to those reported following histopathological evaluation of sections from normal human duodenum (Figure 2C) (Karam, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2C and comparison to published literature.

claim: 305 genes were identified as common and responsible for the closer resemblance of Duodenum Intestine-Chip to human adult duodenum than organoids.
source: We found 305 genes which were common for Duodenum Intestine-Chip and adult duodenum but different from organoids, representing 39.25% of differentially expressed genes in Duodenum Intestine-Chip versus organoids comparison, and 21.22% of differentially expressed genes in human adult duodenal tissue versus organoids comparison (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Biological processes enriched in the 305 overlapping genes were associated with important intestinal functions such as digestion and transport of nutrients and ions, metabolism, detoxification, as well as tissue and tube development.
source: Notably, biological processes enriched in this gene set were associated with important intestinal functions such as digestion and transport of nutrients and ions, metabolism, detoxification, as well as tissue and tube development (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by GO term enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: KEGG Pathway analysis identified a total of seven significantly enriched pathways among the overlapping genes.
source: Additionally, KEGG Pathway analysis identified a total of seven significantly enriched pathways (threshold FDR adjusted p-value<0.05) among the overlapping genes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Many of the enriched pathways were linked to drug metabolism, such as cytochrome CYP450 and metabolism of xenobiotic by cytochrome CYP450.
source: Importantly, many of these pathways were linked to drug metabolism, such as – cytochrome CYP450 (associated with 10 genes), metabolism of xenobiotic by cytochrome CYP450 (associated with 12 genes), and other important pathways related to nutrients absorption and digestion, such as mineral absorption (associated with 12 genes), fat digestion and absorption (associated with nine genes), protein digestion and absorption (associated with 11 genes) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A large number of genes involved in the nutrient absorption, digestion, as well as, metabolism of xenobiotics were highly expressed in Duodenum Intestine-Chip and adult duodenum tissue, but expressed at the low level in organoids.
source: A large number of genes involved in the nutrient absorption, digestion, as well as, metabolism of xenobiotics were highly expressed in Duodenum Intestine-Chip (Chip) and adult duodenum tissue (In vivo), but expressed at the low level in organoids (Organoids).
evidence: This is supported by heatmap analysis of gene expression data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The expression profiles of efflux and uptake drug transporters in Duodenum Intestine-Chip were similar to those observed in human duodenal tissue.
source: The expression profiles of these genes in Duodenum Intestine-Chip were similar to those observed in human duodenal tissue.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Expression of OATP2B1 and OCT1 were markedly increased in Caco-2 Intestine-Chip in comparison to the human duodenum.
source: Although a similar pattern of gene expression was also found in the Caco-2 Intestine-Chip (day 8 of culture), expression of a couple of important organic anion and cation transporters, including OATP2B1 and OCT1, were markedly increased in comparison to the human duodenum.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A 3.5-fold higher expression of MDR1 was found in Caco-2 cells compared with the human duodenum.
source: In line with the trends previously reported by others (Sun et al., 2002; Maubon et al., 2007; Harwood et al., 2016), a 3.5-fold higher expression of MDR1, 3.6-fold and 24-fold lower expression of BCRP and PEPT1, respectively, were found in Caco-2 cells compared with the human duodenum.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data and citations to published literature.

claim: A 3.6-fold lower expression of BCRP was found in Caco-2 cells compared with the human duodenum.
source: In line with the trends previously reported by others (Sun et al., 2002; Maubon et al., 2007; Harwood et al., 2016), a 3.5-fold higher expression of MDR1, 3.6-fold and 24-fold lower expression of BCRP and PEPT1, respectively, were found in Caco-2 cells compared with the human duodenum.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data and citations to published literature.

claim: A 24-fold lower expression of PEPT1 was found in Caco-2 cells compared with the human duodenum.
source: In line with the trends previously reported by others (Sun et al., 2002; Maubon et al., 2007; Harwood et al., 2016), a 3.5-fold higher expression of MDR1, 3.6-fold and 24-fold lower expression of BCRP and PEPT1, respectively, were found in Caco-2 cells compared with the human duodenum.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data and citations to published literature.

claim: MDR1, BCRP and PEPT1 showed in vivo relevant localization at the luminal surface of intestinal epithelium in Duodenum Intestine-Chip.
source: We further demonstrated in vivo relevant localization of the luminal efflux pumps MDR1, more commonly referred to as P-gp or P-glycoprotein (Figure 4B) and BCRP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) as well as the uptake Peptide Transporter 1 (PEPT1) in Duodenum Intestine-Chip (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figures 4B and 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exposure to vinblastine induced a ~2 fold increase in intracellular accumulation of rhodamine in Duodenum Intestine-Chip, confirming the presence of active MDR1 efflux pumps.
source: Exposure to the inhibitor induced a ~ 2 fold increase in intracellular accumulation of rhodamine (1.84-fold increase in Duodenum Intestine-Chip and 2.14-fold increase in Caco-2 cells-based model), confirming the presence of active MDR1 efflux pumps in both cell systems.
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip expressed CYP3A4 at a much higher gene (~6000 times higher, p<0.0001) level than Caco-2 Intestine-Chip.
source: In the present study, we demonstrate that, in comparison to the Caco-2 cells based system, our Duodenum Intestine-Chip expressed CYP3A4 at a much higher gene (~6000 times higher, p<0.0001) (Figure 5A) and protein level (Figure 5B), similar to those observed in the adult human duodenum.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip expressed CYP3A4 at a much higher protein level than Caco-2 Intestine-Chip, similar to those observed in the adult human duodenum.
source: In the present study, we demonstrate that, in comparison to the Caco-2 cells based system, our Duodenum Intestine-Chip expressed CYP3A4 at a much higher gene (~6000 times higher, p<0.0001) (Figure 5A) and protein level (Figure 5B), similar to those observed in the adult human duodenum.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Treatment of Duodenum Intestine-Chip with rifampicin resulted in 5.3-fold induction of CYP3A4 expression relative to DMSO-treated controls.
source: Treatment of Duodenum Intestine-Chip from all three donors with RIF and VD3 resulted in 5.3-fold and 4.1-fold induction of CYP3A4 expression, respectively, relative to that in the DMSO-treated controls (Figure 5C, left).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Treatment of Duodenum Intestine-Chip with vitamin D3 resulted in 4.1-fold induction of CYP3A4 expression relative to DMSO-treated controls.
source: Treatment of Duodenum Intestine-Chip from all three donors with RIF and VD3 resulted in 5.3-fold and 4.1-fold induction of CYP3A4 expression, respectively, relative to that in the DMSO-treated controls (Figure 5C, left).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Caco-2 Intestine-Chip was shown to respond to vitamin D3, but not rifampicin treatment.
source: Alternatively, Caco-2 Intestine-Chip was shown to respond to VD3, but not RIF treatment (Figure 5C, right), which is consistent with the previously published reports (Schmiedlin-Ren et al., 1997; Ozawa et al., 2015; Negoro et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C and citations to published literature.

claim: CYP3A4 was undetectable at the protein level in Caco-2 cells and remained unchanged upon stimulation with rifampicin.
source: Dramatically low baseline expression of CYP3A4 in Caco-2 cells derived system showed to increase by 316-fold in the presence of VD3. However, it did not reach the levels observed in the human tissue and remained undetectable at the protein level as assessed by western blot analysis (Figure 5C, below graph).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The formation of 6β-hydroxytestosterone was higher in Duodenum Intestine-Chip (55.6 ± 7.8 pmol/min/mg protein) compared with Caco-2 Intestine-Chip (4.9 ± 0.64 pmol/min/mg protein).
source: Consistent with the gene and protein expression data, the formation of 6β-OH-T was higher in Duodenum Intestine-Chip (55.6 ± 7.8 pmol/min/mg protein) compared with Caco-2 Intestine-Chip (4.9 ± 0.64 pmol/min/mg protein), and was further increased by RIF (214.4 ± 106.5 pmol/min/mg protein) and VD3 treatment (198.0 ± 41.9 pmol/min/mg protein).
evidence: This is supported by LC-MS data measuring CYP3A4 enzyme activity shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The demonstrated lack of PXR in Caco-2 cells may explain the differences between the Duodenum Intestine-Chip and other Caco-2 cells–based systems.
source: The demonstrated lack of PXR, known to be one of the key transcriptional regulators of CYP3A4 induction in humans, in Caco-2 cells may explain the differences between the Duodenum Intestine-Chip and other Caco-2 cells–based systems, including Caco-2 Intestine-Chip.
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression data and knowledge of CYP3A4 regulation.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip represents an improved human-relevant model for predicting CYP3A4-mediated drug-drug interactions in the intestine for orally delivered drugs, than the commonly used Caco-2 cell-based models.
source: Altogether, our findings support the conclusion that the Duodenum Intestine-Chip represents an improved human-relevant model for predicting CYP3A4-mediated drug-drug interactions in the intestine for orally delivered drugs, than the commonly used Caco-2 cell-based models.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined results of the study.

claim: Caco-2 transwell allow good prediction of transcellular drug absorption.
source: Although many studies have demonstrated that Caco-2 transwell allow good prediction of transcellular drug absorption, they showed to be unreliable in the assessment of passive diffusion of polar molecules such as hydrophilic drugs and peptides.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from published studies.

claim: Caco-2 transwell are unreliable in the assessment of passive diffusion of polar molecules such as hydrophilic drugs and peptides.
source: Although many studies have demonstrated that Caco-2 transwell allow good prediction of transcellular drug absorption, they showed to be unreliable in the assessment of passive diffusion of polar molecules such as hydrophilic drugs and peptides. This is related to much smaller, in respect to small intestinal villi, effective area of the monolayer and its higher tight junctional resistance (Press and Di Grandi, 2008; Kumar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Withdrawal of Wnt3a supplementation leads to a loss of Lgr5-positive cells, decreased cell proliferation, appearance of secretory cell lineages, and the transformation of immature crypt-like enterocytes into differentiated nutrient-absorptive cells.
source: Because human intestinal cells do not produce significant amounts of Wnt3a, EGF, or several other growth factors essential for stem cell division and cell proliferation, removal of Wnt3a supplementation leads to a loss of Lgr5-positive cells, decreased cell proliferation, appearance of secretory cell lineages, including goblet and enteroendocrine cells, and the transformation of immature crypt-like enterocytes into differentiated nutrient-absorptive cells.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about organoid biology.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip could be readily applied beyond ADME applications in development of new approaches and therapeutics that target specific cell populations.
source: Given that we have shown that the Duodenum Intestine-Chip recapitulates faithfully the physiologically relevant ratios of these cells it could be readily applied beyond ADME applications in development of new approaches and therapeutics that target specific cell populations.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential future applications based on the demonstrated capabilities of the model.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip could serve to evaluate specific targeting of Paneth cells, which have been implicated in inflammatory bowel disease.
source: For example, it could serve to evaluate specific targeting of Paneth cells, which through a series of genetic studies have been implicated in inflammatory bowel disease (Xavier and Podolsky, 2007; Khor et al., 2011; Adolph et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is a speculation about potential applications supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The transcriptome of Duodenum Intestine-Chip more closely resembles global gene expression in human adult duodenum than do the organoids.
source: Surprisingly, although chips and organoids were established with the cells of the same origin (donors, source of the tissue) their transcriptomic profiles were shown to significantly differ from each other – the total number of 472 up- and down-regulated genes were found in this comparison. Moreover, several different analyses demonstrated that the transcriptome of Duodenum Intestine-Chip more closely resembles global gene expression in human adult duodenum than do the organoids, strongly suggesting that Duodenum Intestine-Chip constitute a closer approximation of human in vivo tissue.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip could be personalized to assess interindividual differences in drug disposition and responses.
source: Moreover, as it is composed of cells isolated from individual patients, it could be personalized as needed, in order to assess interindividual differences in drug disposition and responses, study the effect of genetic polymorphisms on pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, as well as decoupling the effect of various factors such as age, sex, disease state, and diet on metabolism, clearance, and bioavailability of xenobiotics.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential applications based on the personalized nature of the model.

claim: Duodenum Intestine-Chip could help us to better understand the basic biology of human intestinal tissue in healthy and disease states.
source: This system could also help us to better understand the basic biology of human intestinal tissue in healthy and disease states and potentially enable novel therapeutic development as we further our understanding of the mechanisms driving key disease phenotypes.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential applications of the model.
